Vivek / Marcus — 

Thanks for the ping. High-level response and next steps below — I’ll attach a short redline of the DPA and MSA clauses this morning (file: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20270630.docx).

Summary answers:
1) SCCs: We are comfortable executing the standard EU SCCs (we support both the 2021 and 2024 sets depending on counterparty preference). For CareGrid I recommend proposing the 2024 SCCs but include a fallback to 2021 if they require. Note: we will push to keep auditor access, liability caps, and data export liability language consistent with our standard MSA.

2) Transfer impact / subprocessor locations: We can provide a short transfer-impact addendum stating our subprocessor categories, primary regions (US, EU, APAC), and that onward transfers happen only under SCCs or equivalent safeguards. We should avoid granular IP addresses — instead provide named subprocessors and an up-to-date list link.

3) Evidence pack: SOC 2 Type II (most recent) and our data retention + incident response summary are available. Marcus — please confirm SOC 2 file name and whether we can share a redacted audit summary.

Outstanding legal asks (I will put as comments in the redline):
- Customer wants to change "Processor" obligations to include independent verification rights beyond SOC 2 — we should offer quarterly security questionnaires instead of full access.
- Narrow the breach notice timing and preserve our 7-day assessment window before notification.

I created SUP-1234 to track this redline and the DocuSign flow. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234

I’ll circulate the redline and a one-page transfer note by EOD. If CareGrid needs faster turnaround, propose a 30-minute call with their counsel.

— Priyom
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
